name: Plaza de Armas de Urubamba
note: The central civic square of Urubamba, framed by the town’s street grid and San Pedro Apóstol church. A useful starting point for exploring the markets and public places around the center.

photo.alt: San Pedro church and its steps on the northern edge of Urubamba’s Plaza de Armas, September 2018; a view of the square’s church frontage
photo.author: James Challco Palomino

name: Iglesia San Pedro Apóstol
note: The Catholic parish church facing Urubamba’s main square. Its broad stone frontage, tiered bell wall, entrance steps, and tiled nave roof are visible in the photographed present-day building.

photo.alt: Stone facade and stepped bell wall of San Pedro Apóstol church in Urubamba, October 2019
photo.author: Alexey Komarov

name: Santuario del Señor de Torrechayoc
note: The sanctuary north of the town center is associated with Urubamba’s devotion to the Señor de Torrechayoc. The annual festival brings together religious processions, music, and local dance traditions.

name: Mercado Modelo de Urubamba
note: The covered central market west of the main square. Local traders sell food and everyday provisions here; the interior photograph shows its aisles, upper gallery, and produce stalls.

photo.alt: Interior aisles and stalls of Mercado Modelo de Urubamba, August 2026
photo.author: Yupanasimi

name: Mercado de Productores de Urubamba
note: A separate producers’ market west of the center, connecting Urubamba with growers from across the province. The municipal anniversary festival highlights local agricultural products and food traditions.

photo.alt: Produce stalls during the Wednesday fair at Mercado de Productores in Urubamba, 26 August 2026
photo.author: Yupanasimi

name: Qespiwanka · Palacio de Huayna Cápac
note: Surviving remains of the palace associated with Inca ruler Wayna Qhapaq, on the northern side of Urubamba. The atlas marks the mapped ruin footprint; it does not reconstruct the palace in its inhabited form.

name: Museo de Qespiwanka
note: In the restored Casa Hacienda Pino, five exhibition rooms explore the Qhapaq Ñan road network, Qespiwanka palace, and Urubamba’s living traditions. This museum is distinct from the nearby palace ruins.
